legend: The only difference between easy and hard versions is constraints.

You are given n%%ZSMJ0%% segments on the coordinate axis OX%%ZSMJ1%%. Segments can intersect, lie inside each other and even coincide. The i%%ZSMJ2%%-th segment is [li;ri]%%ZSMJ3%% (li≤ri%%ZSMJ4%%) and it covers all integer points j%%ZSMJ5%% such that li≤j≤ri%%ZSMJ6%%.
The integer point is called bad if it is covered by strictly more than k%%ZSMJ7%% segments.
Your task is to remove the minimum number of segments so that there are no bad points at all.
input: The first line of the input contains two integers n%%ZSMJ8%% and k%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤k≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ10%%) — the number of segments and the maximum number of segments by which each integer point can be covered.
The next n%%ZSMJ11%% lines contain segments. The i%%ZSMJ12%%-th line contains two integers li%%ZSMJ13%% and ri%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤li≤ri≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ15%%) — the endpoints of the i%%ZSMJ16%%-th segment.
output: In the first line print one integer m%%ZSMJ17%% (0≤m≤n%%ZSMJ18%%) — the minimum number of segments you need to remove so that there are no bad points.
In the second line print m%%ZSMJ19%% distinct integers p1,p2,…,pm%%ZSMJ20%% (1≤pi≤n%%ZSMJ21%%) — indices of segments you remove in any order. If there are multiple answers, you can print any of them.
